original_question: (Well-known problem). A classifying space for a group G is a connected CW complex with fundamental group G and all higher homotopy groups trivial. A group is of type Fn if it has a classifying space with finite n-skeleton. For example, type F1 is equivalent to finite generation, and type F2 is equivalent to finite presentability. Type F∞ means type Fn for all n. For n ⩾ 3, does every group of type Fn−1 embed as a subgroup of a group of type Fn? Or even in a group of type F∞?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.146 ("Well-known problem") in the section New Problems (21st issue, 2026), page 181. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already reproduces the paper's setup and question almost verbatim: it defines a classifying space, states the definition of type F_n, notes the standard identifications F_1 = finite generation and F_2 = finite presentability, explains F_∞, and asks exactly the same embedding question for n ≥ 3, including the stronger follow-up asking about embedding into a group of type F_∞. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: Make the quantifier fully explicit: fix an integer n ≥ 3, and ask whether the statement holds for every group G of type F_{n-1}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
State that type F_n means the existence of some classifying space K(G,1) with finite n-skeleton. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
Spell out that "embed as a subgroup" means there exists an injective homomorphism G → H into a group H of the indicated finiteness type. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Make clear that the second sentence is a stronger version of the same question: can H always be chosen of type F_∞? The paper does not present this as an equivalent reformulation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Do not add any extra hypotheses such as torsion-freeness, countability, coherence, or finite presentability beyond what is forced by G being of type F_{n-1}; the problem statement in the paper imposes none. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: Fix an integer n ≥ 3. If G is an abstract group of type F_{n-1}, meaning that G admits a classifying space K(G,1) with finite (n-1)-skeleton, must there exist a group H of type F_n and an injective homomorphism G → H? More strongly, can H always be chosen to be of type F_∞? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

The only faithful sharpening needed is to make the universal quantifier in n and the injective-embedding formulation explicit, while avoiding any broadening beyond the notebook's wording.
